canonical_record.label: Howard et al. confidence sequences over unbounded horizons
canonical_record.summary: Howard et al. report constructing shrinking confidence sequences with time-uniform, nonasymptotic coverage under nonparametric conditions.

statement: Howard et al. report constructing shrinking confidence sequences with time-uniform, nonasymptotic coverage under nonparametric conditions.

scope.assumptions: Guarantees require the authors' stated conditions
scope.uncertainty: Coverage level not given in abstract

support.quote: A confidence sequence is a sequence of confidence intervals that is uniformly valid over an unbounded time horizon. Our work develops confidence sequences whose widths go to zero, with nonasymptotic coverage guarantees under nonparametric conditions.

canonical_record.label: Vovk and Wang e-value averaging
canonical_record.summary: Vovk and Wang report that multiple e-values for one hypothesis can be merged by averaging them.

statement: Vovk and Wang report that multiple e-values for one hypothesis can be merged by averaging them.

scope.population: Tests of a common null hypothesis
scope.assumptions: Inputs must be valid e-values for the same null
scope.uncertainty: Dependence and construction details not in abstract

support.quote: We demonstrate that e-values are often mathematically more tractable; in particular, in multiple testing of a single hypothesis, e-values can be merged simply by averaging them. This allows us to develop efficient procedures using e-values for testing multiple hypotheses.

canonical_record.label: Xu and Ramdas e-LOND dependence-robust online FDR
canonical_record.summary: Xu and Ramdas report e-LOND control of online false discovery rate under arbitrary, possibly unknown, dependence.

statement: Xu and Ramdas report e-LOND control of online false discovery rate under arbitrary, possibly unknown, dependence.

scope.uncertainty: No quantitative FDR threshold in abstract

support.quote: Our algorithm, e-LOND, provides FDR control under arbitrary, possibly unknown, dependence.

canonical_record.label: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas bounded-mean betting inference
canonical_record.summary: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas report martingale-based confidence intervals and time-uniform sequences for bounded means, including sampling without replacement and adaptation to unknown variance.

sources.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting

statement: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas report martingale-based confidence intervals and time-uniform sequences for bounded means, including sampling without replacement and adaptation to unknown variance.

scope.uncertainty: Exact validity conditions not given in abstract

support.quote: This paper derives confidence intervals (CI) and time-uniform confidence sequences (CS) for the classical problem of estimating an unknown mean from bounded observations.

At its heart, it is based on a class of composite nonnegative martingales, with strong connections to testing by betting and the method of mixtures. We show how to extend these ideas to sampling without replacement, another heavily studied problem. In all cases, our bounds are adaptive to the unknown variance

canonical_record.label: Choe and Ramdas filtration-mismatch warning
canonical_record.summary: Choe and Ramdas report that e-process validity in a coarser filtration does not automatically hold in a finer filtration, preventing unadjusted averaging across them.

statement: Choe and Ramdas report that e-process validity in a coarser filtration does not automatically hold in a finer filtration, preventing unadjusted averaging across them.

support.quote: Although e-processes in the same filtration can be combined effortlessly (by averaging), e-processes in different filtrations cannot because their validity in a coarser filtration does not translate to a finer filtration.

canonical_record.label: Choe and Ramdas adjust-then-combine procedure
canonical_record.summary: Choe and Ramdas report an adjust-then-combine procedure lifting e-processes across filtrations, with a logarithmic validity-recovery cost.

statement: Choe and Ramdas report an adjust-then-combine procedure lifting e-processes across filtrations, with a logarithmic validity-recovery cost.

scope.assumptions: Use suitable adjusters for the same null
scope.uncertainty: No numerical cost constants in abstract

support.quote: We establish that a class of functions called adjusters can lift arbitrary e-processes across filtrations. The result yields a generally applicable "adjust-then-combine" procedure
Second, when we coarsen the filtration to construct an e-process, there is a logarithmic cost to recovering validity in the original filtration.

canonical_record.label: Dwork et al. reusable holdout for adaptive validation
canonical_record.summary: Dwork et al. report that adaptive holdout reuse risks overfitting and propose an algorithm to validate many adaptively chosen hypotheses while avoiding that overfitting.

sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse

statement: Dwork et al. report that adaptive holdout reuse risks overfitting and propose an algorithm to validate many adaptively chosen hypotheses while avoiding that overfitting.

support.quote: Reusing a holdout set adaptively multiple times can easily lead to overfitting to the holdout set itself. We give an algorithm that enables the validation of a large number of adaptively chosen hypotheses, while provably avoiding overfitting.

canonical_record.label: Lee et al. selection-conditional inference for lasso
canonical_record.summary: Lee et al. report selection-conditional inference for lasso-selected coefficients, including confidence intervals and tests.

sources.title: Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso

statement: Lee et al. report selection-conditional inference for lasso-selected coefficients, including confidence intervals and tests.

support.quote: At the core of our framework is a result that characterizes the distribution of a post-selection estimator conditioned on the selection event. We specialize the approach to model selection by the lasso to form valid confidence intervals for the selected coefficients and test whether all relevant variables have been included in the model.

canonical_record.label: Ramdas et al. necessity of martingales for admissible anytime-valid inference
canonical_record.summary: Ramdas et al. report that all admissible confidence sequences, p-processes and e-processes rely on nonnegative martingales under their formal admissibility definition.

sources.title: Admissible anytime-valid sequential inference must rely on nonnegative martingales

statement: Ramdas et al. report that all admissible confidence sequences, p-processes and e-processes rely on nonnegative martingales under their formal admissibility definition.

support.quote: Our central contribution is to show that nonnegative martingales are also universal
we show that all admissible constructions of confidence sequences, p-processes, or e-processes must necessarily utilize nonnegative martingales.
